title: In-Situ Investigations of Tensile and Fracture Behavior of Lattice Structures for Advanced Reactor Applications
content: Currently, there is a significant opportunity in developing materials for nuclear reactors, as future advanced reactors demand new materials that balance high-temperature resilience, mechanical strength, and reduced weight. This is especially relevant for commercial, defense, and aerospace applications where reactor mobility is essential. Topologically designed lattice structures can dramatically reduce the weight of bulk structural components while retaining most of the base material’s properties. Efforts are currently underway at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) to design lattice structures for advanced reactors.
